verdict.root_cause: Frontend request handlers stall to a fixed ~15s client deadline while emitting nothing themselves. In 8 of 10 sampled traces the frontend span consumes nearly the whole trace as self-time with no child spans, and the ERROR marks sit on the wrapping frontend-proxy ingress and load-generator client spans, whose own self-time is ~0ms [tr_838e5c9acc04]. Frontend's own error ratio stays flat at zero [tr_4bec7214ac16] — it is not failing requests, it is not answering them — while the proxy's error ratio steps off a zero-variance baseline at 02:25:46 [tr_4bfa31fa6797]. Durations cluster on one ~15.000s value rather than spreading, a deadline cutoff rather than queueing [tr_838e5c9acc04], and no deploy, config push or flag flip exists for frontend or its one-hop neighbours [tr_6ab4975b4cff, tr_5e7448476208]. Socket still accepting, callers hanging to their deadline, no outbound work attempted, nothing changed: a frozen frontend process, likely a subset of replicas since some ad and /api/cart requests still complete in milliseconds [tr_838e5c9acc04].
verdict.reasoning: The alert started at frontend-proxy, but the proxy only wraps the long frontend span with ~0ms self-time, so time is lost inside the frontend handler [tr_838e5c9acc04]. The stalled spans have no children at all, so no downstream call was ever issued — that removes dependency_latency as the mechanism, and the cart/ad/Redis calls that do appear finish under 3ms. Those same healthy outbound calls show frontend's network path is intact, separating this from network_partition. The fixed ~15.000s clustering and the step onset from a zero-variance baseline rule out the ramp shape of resource_exhaustion [tr_838e5c9acc04, tr_4bfa31fa6797]. The empty change log removes bad_deploy, bad_config and feature_flag as recorded acts [tr_6ab4975b4cff, tr_5e7448476208]. A process that accepts and then does nothing is a freeze; the fix is restarting the affected instances.
open_questions: Frontend's log silence is weak evidence: the gap covers the whole pre-incident baseline hour and frontend-proxy is equally empty [tr_c665ffa355cd, tr_4020e752193a], so a label mismatch or ingestion outage is as likely as the process writing nothing.

Frontend CPU, memory, restarts, thread/FD saturation and request rate were never measured [tr_4bec7214ac16]; a pegged CPU or deadlocked thread pool would look identical in traces and would reclassify this as resource_exhaustion.
Triage flagged one unmeasured edge; if frontend makes an uninstrumented outbound call, 'no child spans' is an instrumentation artefact rather than proof no downstream work was attempted.

alternatives.root_cause: Frontend exhausted a bounded resource (thread pool, connections, CPU) so requests queue unserved until the caller's 15s deadline.
alternatives.why_not: Affected spans land on one near-identical ~15.000s value and the proxy error ratio steps rather than ramps [tr_838e5c9acc04, tr_4bfa31fa6797]; saturation normally produces a spread of elevated durations. No frontend saturation metric was collected, so this stays live.

alternatives.root_cause: Frontend stalls on an uninstrumented downstream dependency that is itself slow, with the call invisible in traces.
alternatives.why_not: Every instrumented dependency call in the same traces completes under 3ms and the stalled spans emit no children at all [tr_838e5c9acc04]; this requires assuming the one unmeasured edge hides the whole fault.

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating the frontend container should clear whatever in-process state is holding its request handlers. Observable within one or two 5m rate windows: (1) frontend-proxy's span-metrics error ratio falls back to the zero-variance baseline it held for the full pre-incident hour and stops producing the bursts that peaked near 25% [tr_4bfa31fa6797]; (2) new traces for the browser-facing GET routes (user_browse_product, user_get_recommendations, the initial GET of user_add_to_cart) and the checkout POST no longer show frontend spans clustered on ~15.000s of pure self-time with zero children, and instead resemble the healthy legs already seen in the same window (/api/cart, AdService/GetAds, CartService calls in single-digit ms) [tr_838e5c9acc04]; (3) ERROR status stops being marked on the wrapping frontend-proxy/ingress and load-generator client spans. Frontend's own error ratio should remain flat at zero throughout, since it was never the thing emitting errors [tr_4bec7214ac16] — a jump there after the restart would itself be a bad sign.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, 7 minutes after the recreate, traces still show frontend spans pinned at ~15.000s with no child spans, or frontend-proxy's error ratio has not returned to zero. That would mean the stall is not a one-off frozen process but is being re-induced by ongoing conditions — the two live alternatives named as open: (a) resource exhaustion (pegged CPU, deadlocked or exhausted thread pool) under steady load-generator traffic, which would reproduce within minutes of the fresh process taking traffic, and which was never measured because frontend CPU/memory/restarts/FDs were not queried [tr_4bec7214ac16]; or (b) an uninstrumented outbound call from frontend, in which case 'no child spans' was an instrumentation artefact and the real stall is downstream of frontend, untouched by this restart [tr_838e5c9acc04]. Also partially unfalsifiable from logs: frontend and frontend-proxy return zero log lines across the whole window including the baseline hour [tr_c665ffa355cd, tr_4020e752193a], so 'frontend starts logging again' cannot be used as a success signal — confirmation must come from traces and the proxy error ratio only.
proposal.risk: Not harmless. The restart is irreversible and discards in-process state — cache only for this world's services, so expect a cold-cache latency bump on frontend's first requests that could briefly look like the symptom returning; do not read the first 60s of elevated latency as failure. If the diagnosis is wrong and the cause is resource exhaustion driven by load, the restart buys a few minutes and then the stall returns, having destroyed the frozen process's state — the thread dumps, FD counts and memory profile that would have distinguished a deadlock from a freeze are gone, and the next investigator has strictly less to work with. If the cause is an uninstrumented downstream dependency, this restarts a healthy service and leaves the real fault running. There is also a measurement hazard: the 15s cluster is a client-side deadline cutoff, so if only a subset of replicas is frozen and the recreate does not replace that subset, the error ratio may improve partially and be misread as a fix.
proposal.blast_radius: One service, for the duration of the container recreate. frontend-proxy is the direct inbound caller and will see connection resets or 5xx on in-flight and newly arriving requests while frontend is down; load-generator sits above it and will record those as client-side errors, briefly pushing frontend-proxy's error ratio up before it falls. That transient spike is expected and must not be confused with the incident signal — judge success on the ratio several minutes after the recreate, not during it. In-flight user-facing requests on the browser page routes and the checkout POST are dropped. No other service in the blast radius is touched directly; the ad and cart backends simply see frontend's traffic pause and resume.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alert on the edge proxy with the load generator simultaneously affected indicates user-facing impact, not an isolated synthetic signal. No open incident covers it, and the alerts alone don't point to a specific fault class.
